docs.title: susshi 🍣
docs.text:
susshi is a terminal-based SSH connection manager written in Rust — hierarchical YAML inventory, Catppuccin-themed TUI, jump hosts, Wallix bastions, tunnels, and SCP in one place.

Get Started View on GitHub

docs.title: Why susshi?
docs.text:
Managing dozens or hundreds of hosts with a single ~/.ssh/config quickly becomes fragile: no centralized visibility, no interactive interface, limited grouping, and poor ergonomics for day-to-day tasks.

susshi addresses these gaps:

  • Ergonomics & speed — fuzzy search, keyboard-driven navigation, one-key connect. No editing files and re-running commands.
  • Infrastructure visibility — hierarchical groups, favorites, tag filters, interactive inventory at a glance.
  • Bastion & multi-hop workflows — automatic orchestration of jump hops and Wallix integration without repetitive ssh_config entries.
  • Inventory management — variable inheritance, environment profiles, YAML includes, and exports to Ansible/Terraform/Nmap/CSV.
  • Built-in operations — tunnels, SCP, pre/post-connect hooks, --validate checks.
  • Security & privacy — local-first, no cloud dependency, no telemetry.

docs.title: Configuration Guide
docs.text: susshi reads ~/.susshi.yml by default. This page documents the full schema and inheritance model.

docs.title: Configuration Inheritance
docs.text:
Settings are resolved with this priority (highest last):

  1. defaults
  2. group
  3. environment
  4. server

docs.title: Field semantics by inheritance level
docs.text:
Not all fields follow the same rule. Three distinct semantics apply:

Semantic Fields Behaviour OVERRIDE user, ssh_key, ssh_cert, ssh_agent_sock, ssh_port, mode, ssh_options, wallix, jump, production Lower level replaces the parent value entirely REPLACE tunnels Lower level replaces the parent list entirely; if absent the parent list is used UNION tags, probe_filesystems Every level appends its values to the parent list (duplicates are removed)

Fields only available in defaults (not overridable per group/env/server): theme, keep_open, default_filter, use_system_ssh_config, control_master, agent_forwarding, control_path, control_persist, pre_connect_hook, post_disconnect_hook, hook_timeout_secs, confirm_production.

docs.title: includes (Multi-file Configuration)
docs.text:
Use includes to split configuration by team, perimeter, or environment:

includes:
  - label: "DEV"
    path: "~/.susshi_dev.yml"
  - label: "QUALIF"
    path: "~/.susshi_qualif.yml"
    merge_defaults: true

Fields:

  • label: displayed as a namespace header in the TUI.
  • path: absolute path, ~-expanded path, or a https:// / http:// URL.
  • merge_defaults (optional, default: false): merge main-file defaults as base values for the included file.

docs.title: HTTPS includes
docs.text:
path can be a full HTTPS URL. susshi will fetch the file over TLS at startup:

includes:
  - label: "SHARED"
    path: "https://inventory.example.com/team-servers.yml"
    merge_defaults: true

Behavior:

  • The URL is fetched synchronously at startup (same point as file includes).
  • HTTP errors and network failures are non-fatal — emitted as LoadError warnings.
  • The downloaded content is validated with the same unknown-field checks as local files.
  • Recursive includes inside a URL-fetched file use normal local-path resolution.

Behavior (all includes):

  • Includes are resolved recursively.
  • Circular includes are reported as non-blocking warnings.
  • Missing/unreadable files are non-fatal warnings.
  • Unknown YAML fields emit non-blocking ValidationWarning entries.

docs.title: defaults
docs.text: Global values applied unless overridden. See the field availability table above for the full list.

docs.title: Jump block
docs.text:
jump is always a list (even for one host). The entire list is replaced by a child level that defines jump:

jump:
  - host: "jump1.example.com"
    user: "jump-user"
  - host: "jump2.example.com"    # multi-hop: second hop
    user: "jump-user"

docs.title: Wallix block
docs.text:
wallix:
  host: "bastion.example.com"
  user: "bastion-user"
  group: "devops-admins"
  account: "default"
  protocol: "SSH"
  auto_select: true
  fail_if_menu_match_error: true
  selection_timeout_secs: 8
  # direct: false          # menu flow only: skip menu probe for direct-checkout targets
  # authorization: ""      # force exact Wallix authorization name (skips menu matching)
  # authorizations: ["PR-APP_{group}"]  # candidate authorizations, {group} = suffix above
  # header_columns: ["ID", "Cible", "Autorisation"]  # override if bastion uses different column labels

bastion is accepted as a backward-compatible alias key.

Wallix-specific fields:

  • template — login-string template. Default: {target_user}@%n:SSH:{bastion_user}.
  • direct — skip the menu probe in the menu flow. No effect when an authorization is known (the direct login is used).
  • authorization — force the exact Wallix authorization name. Skips menu matching when set.
  • authorizations — candidate authorization names, in order of preference; {group} is replaced by group. A single candidate enables the direct login (no menu); several are tried in order. See Wallix Guide.
  • header_columns — list of tokens used to detect the menu header row. Override if your bastion uses localized or custom column names.

docs.title: Tunnels
docs.text:
Tunnels use REPLACE semantics: a child level that defines tunnels replaces the parent list entirely. This allows per-environment or per-server tunnel sets without inheriting unwanted parent tunnels.

tunnels:
  - local_port: 5432
    remote_host: 127.0.0.1
    remote_port: 5432
    label: "PostgreSQL"     # optional — auto-generated if absent

In wallix mode, tunnels require a known Wallix authorization — see Tunnels.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
Tags use UNION semantics: every level (defaults → group → env → server) appends its tags to the accumulated set. Duplicates are removed (first occurrence wins).

defaults:
  tags: [infra]
groups:
  - name: Prod
    tags: [prod]
    environments:
      - name: EU
        tags: [eu-west]
        servers:
          - name: web-01
            host: 10.0.0.1
            tags: [web]
# web-01 resolved tags: [infra, prod, eu-west, web]

Tags can be used to filter servers in the TUI (/) or in --export-filter.

docs.title: Production servers
docs.text:
Servers flagged as production get a red PROD badge in the list and the status bar, and a red border with a ⚠ PRODUCTION line in the details panel.

  • Explicit flag: production: true|false at any level (defaults, group, environment, server). The most specific level wins, so a server can opt out of a production environment.
  • Auto-detection (fallback when no level sets the flag): the environment name is prod, production or prd (case-insensitive). Names such as preprod or product-api do not match.
  • Confirmation (opt-in): set confirm_production: true in defaults to be asked before connecting to a production server. Only y confirms; n or Esc cancels (Enter is ignored on purpose, so a reflex double-press cannot bypass it).
defaults:
  confirm_production: true

groups:
  - name: Shop
    environments:
      - name: prod          # auto-detected
        servers:
          - name: web-1
            host: 203.0.113.10
      - name: staging
        production: true    # explicit flag
        servers:
          - name: web-stg
            host: 203.0.113.20

docs.title: _vars and Interpolation
docs.text:
Define per-file variables:

_vars:
  bastion: "bastion.prod.example.com"
  env: "prod"

Use placeholders in any string field:

name: "api-{{ env }}"
host: "{{ bastion }}"

Rules:

  • Scope is file-local (does not leak across includes).
  • Undefined variables emit a non-blocking warning and leave the {{ placeholder }} intact.
  • Built-in {{ index }} expands to the 1-based server position within each list.

docs.title: groups, environments, and servers
docs.text:
Top-level inventory is defined in groups.

A group can contain:

  • servers directly (level 2: Group → Server), or
  • nested environments, each with servers (level 3: Group → Environment → Server).

Any level may override defaults.

docs.title: Server-specific fields
docs.text:
• name, host — required
  • mode — direct, jump, or wallix
  • tags — string labels, merged with parent tags (UNION)
  • notes — free-form description shown in the detail panel
  • ssh_key — path to the private key (tilde expanded)
  • ssh_cert — path to a signed SSH certificate passed alongside ssh_key
  • ssh_agent_sock — path to a Unix socket for a dedicated SSH agent (Unix only)
  • tunnels — predefined local-port-forwarding tunnels (REPLACE semantics)
  • pre_connect_hook, post_disconnect_hook — server-level hook overrides

docs.title: Create your first inventory
docs.text:
Create ~/.susshi.yml:

defaults:
  user: "your-user"
  ssh_key: "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"

groups:
  - name: "My Servers"
    servers:
      - name: "web-01"
        host: "192.168.1.10"
        mode: "direct"
      - name: "db-01"
        host: "192.168.1.20"
        mode: "direct"

docs.title: Launch the TUI
docs.text:
susshi

You'll see your server list. Navigate with j/k, press Enter to connect, / to search.

docs.title: Essential keybindings
docs.text: Key Action j / k or ↓ / ↑ Move down / up Enter Connect or toggle group / Fuzzy search Tab Switch mode (Direct / Jump / Wallix) f Toggle favorite F Show favorites only T Tunnel manager E Expand all groups h Keyboard help overlay q Quit

docs.text: susshi --direct your-user@192.168.1.10

docs.title: Validate your config
docs.text:
susshi --validate

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: susshi can execute shell scripts before and after each SSH connection.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Set hooks at any config level (defaults, group, environment, server). Lower levels override higher ones.

defaults:
  pre_connect_hook: "~/.config/susshi/hooks/pre_connect.sh"
  post_disconnect_hook: "~/.config/susshi/hooks/post_disconnect.sh"
  hook_timeout_secs: 5
Field Description pre_connect_hook Path to script executed before the SSH connection opens post_disconnect_hook Path to script executed after the SSH connection closes hook_timeout_secs Max seconds to wait for a hook to complete (default: 5)

A non-zero exit code from pre_connect_hook cancels the connection.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
The following variables are set when the hook runs:

Variable Value SUSSHI_SERVER Server name as declared in the config SUSSHI_HOST Resolved hostname or IP SUSSHI_USER SSH user SUSSHI_PORT SSH port SUSSHI_MODE Connection mode: direct, jump, or wallix

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Bash — log connections:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "$(date -Iseconds) connect $SUSSHI_USER@$SUSSHI_HOST ($SUSSHI_SERVER)" \
  >> ~/.local/share/susshi/connections.log

Fish — notify on connect:

#!/usr/bin/env fish
notify-send "susshi" "Connecting to $SUSSHI_SERVER ($SUSSHI_HOST)"

Pre-connect guard — block production servers outside business hours:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [[ "$SUSSHI_MODE" == "wallix" ]]; then
  hour=$(date +%H)
  if (( hour < 8 || hour > 18 )); then
    echo "Production connections blocked outside 08:00–18:00" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi
exit 0

Make hook scripts executable: chmod +x ~/.config/susshi/hooks/*.sh

docs.title: Import from OpenSSH Config
docs.text:
Generate susshi YAML from an existing ~/.ssh/config:

susshi --import-ssh-config
susshi --import-ssh-config --dry-run                        # preview without writing
susshi --import-ssh-config --output ~/.susshi.yml           # write to specific file
susshi --import-ssh-config --ssh-config-path ~/work/.ssh/config

Behavior:

  • Recursive Include directives are followed.
  • ProxyJump entries are converted to jump-mode configuration.
  • The output is printed to stdout unless --output is specified.

docs.title: List Servers as JSON
docs.text:
Print all resolved servers as a JSON array — ready for jq or fzf pipelines:

susshi --list
susshi --list --list-filter "web"
susshi --list --list-filter "#prod"

Each object contains: name, host, user, port, group, env, namespace, tags, mode.

Example pipelines:

# Pick a server with fzf and connect
susshi --list | jq -r '.[].name' | fzf | xargs -I{} susshi --direct {}

# Show all hostnames tagged prod
susshi --list --list-filter "#prod" | jq -r '.[].host'

docs.title: Export Inventory
docs.text: All export commands support --export-filter with the same text and #tag syntax as the TUI search bar. Output goes to stdout unless --export-output <file> is specified.

docs.title: Ansible
docs.text:
susshi --export ansible
susshi --export ansible --export-output ~/inventory.yml
susshi --export ansible --export-filter "#prod"

Produces a standard Ansible YAML inventory with groups mapped from susshi groups and environments.

docs.title: Terraform
docs.text:
susshi --export terraform
susshi --export terraform --export-output inventory.json
susshi --export terraform --export-filter "#prod"

Produces a JSON file loadable with jsondecode(file(...)):

locals {
  susshi = jsondecode(file("${path.module}/inventory.json"))
}

resource "null_resource" "ping" {
  for_each = { for s in local.susshi.servers : s.name => s }
  # each.value.host, each.value.user, each.value.port, …
}

docs.title: Nmap / masscan
docs.text:
susshi --export nmap
susshi --export nmap --export-output targets.txt
susshi --export nmap --export-filter "#prod"

nmap -iL targets.txt -p 22 -sV
masscan -iL targets.txt -p 22

docs.title: CSV
docs.text:
Columns: name, host, user, port, ssh_key, group, env, namespace, tags, notes.

susshi --export csv
susshi --export csv --export-output ~/servers.csv
susshi --export csv --export-filter "#prod"

Fields with commas, double-quotes, or newlines are quoted per RFC 4180. Multiple tags are joined with ;.

docs.title: OpenSSH Config
docs.text:
Exports servers as Host blocks compatible with ~/.ssh/config:

susshi --export openssh
susshi --export openssh --export-output ~/.ssh/config.d/susshi
susshi --export openssh --export-filter "#prod"

Each server produces a Host block with HostName, User, Port (if not 22), IdentityFile, ProxyJump (jump mode), and IdentityAgent (if ssh_agent_sock is set). Wallix servers are exported as direct blocks — their bastion routing is not representable in standard SSH config.

docs.title: SCP File Transfers
docs.text: susshi provides an in-TUI form for uploading and downloading files to the selected server.

docs.title: Opening the SCP Form
docs.text:
Press s when a server is selected, then choose the direction:

Key Direction ↑ / u Upload (local → server) ↓ / d Download (server → local)

docs.title: Form Fields
docs.text:
Field Description Local Local file (upload) or destination path (download) Remote Remote destination (upload) or remote file (download) — pre-filled with user@host:~

Tab switches field, Enter starts the transfer, Esc cancels.

Remote paths:

  • ~ and ~/… are relative to the remote home directory.
  • A path ending with / is treated as a directory: the local file name is appended.

docs.title: Transfer Progress
docs.text: The transfer runs in the background: a progress bar with the transferred size and ETA is shown in the status panel while you keep using the TUI. When it ends, a result popup shows the outcome (long error messages wrap); close it with Enter or Esc.

docs.title: How Transfers Run
docs.text:
Mode Engine Direct Native SFTP/SCP over libssh2 (agent, ssh_key, then default keys) Jump Native, through the first jump host (direct-tcpip channel) Wallix System scp binary, see below

After an upload, susshi checks the server acknowledgement: a remote write error (permission denied, full disk…) is reported instead of a false success.

docs.title: Wallix mode
docs.text:
susshi runs the system scp with the direct Wallix login:

scp -A … user@target+SSH+AUTHORIZATION+bastion_user@bastion:path
  • Authorizations come from the configuration (wallix.authorization, then wallix.authorizations), tried in order while Wallix answers Cible invalide; the name derived from the YAML structure (<ENV>-<GROUP>_<group>) is only a last resort. See Wallix Guide.
  • Agent forwarding (-A) lets the bastion authenticate on the target with your SSH agent: your key must be loaded in the agent (ssh-add -l). No password prompt is possible (BatchMode).
  • scp runs on a pseudo-terminal so its progress meter drives the progress bar. On download the file size is unknown: only the percentage is shown, without size, speed or ETA.
  • On failure, the error shows the scp message (without OpenSSH warnings) and the exact target used, to compare with a manual scp.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The transfer uses the same SSH parameters as the selected server (key, port, jump, agent socket, ssh_options in Wallix mode).
  • For large or automated transfers, use rsync or scp directly with the SSH command copied via y.

docs.title: SSH Certificates (ssh_cert)
docs.text:
Pass a signed SSH certificate alongside the private key:

servers:
  - name: bastion-jump
    host: jump.example.com
    ssh_key: "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"
    ssh_cert: "~/.ssh/id_ed25519-cert.pub"

susshi passes both as -i <ssh_key> -i <ssh_cert> to the ssh binary. Use this when your CA signs short-lived certificates for authentication.

docs.title: SSH Agent Socket (ssh_agent_sock)
docs.text:
Route a server's connections through a dedicated SSH agent socket instead of the default SSH_AUTH_SOCK:

servers:
  - name: secure-host
    host: 198.51.100.50
    ssh_agent_sock: "/run/user/1000/gnupg/S.gpg-agent.ssh"

susshi sets SSH_AUTH_SOCK to the given path and passes -o IdentityAgent=<path> to ssh. Useful for:

  • GPG-based SSH agents (e.g., gpg-agent with enable-ssh-support)
  • Per-server agent isolation (different keys for different environments)

Unix only. Has no effect on Windows.

docs.title: Agent Forwarding (agent_forwarding)
docs.text:
Enable SSH agent forwarding with the -A flag:

defaults:
  agent_forwarding: false  # default

groups:
  - name: "Jump Infrastructure"
    agent_forwarding: true

Inheritable at any config level. Avoid enabling globally — forward only to hosts you trust.

docs.title: SSH ControlMaster
docs.text:
Reuse SSH connections for the same host. Subsequent connections open nearly instantly without a new handshake.

defaults:
  control_master: true
  control_path: "~/.ssh/ctl/%h_%p_%r"  # default socket location
  control_persist: "10m"               # keep master alive 10 min after disconnect

susshi automatically creates the parent directory of the socket path.

Note: ControlMaster is not supported in Wallix mode and is automatically disabled for those connections.

docs.title: Extra SSH Options (ssh_options)
docs.text:
Pass arbitrary ssh -o options at any config level:

defaults:
  ssh_options:
    - "StrictHostKeyChecking=no"
    - "UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null"

groups:
  - name: "Trusted LAN"
    ssh_options:
      - "StrictHostKeyChecking=yes"

Options at a lower level replace the inherited list entirely. To extend the parent list, repeat the inherited options alongside the new ones.

docs.title: System SSH Config (use_system_ssh_config)
docs.text:
Let ssh resolve hosts, users, and ports from ~/.ssh/config:

defaults:
  use_system_ssh_config: false  # default

When true, susshi does not suppress ~/.ssh/config — the standard SSH config file is applied for all connections. Useful when you already have a rich ~/.ssh/config and want susshi to complement it rather than replace it.

docs.title: In-TUI Diagnostics
docs.text:
Press d when a server is selected to run a quick diagnostic probe over SSH.

The overlay displays:

  • Kernel version and OS info
  • CPU model and core count
  • Load average (1 min, 5 min, 15 min)
  • RAM usage bar (used / total)
  • Disk usage bars for / and any extra paths in probe_filesystems
  • A ⚠ warning for any configured filesystem that is not mounted

The probe uses the current connection mode (Direct, Jump or Wallix). In Wallix mode it goes through the direct login, like SCP — see wallix.md.

docs.title: Verbose Mode
docs.text: Press v in the TUI (or pass --verbose on the CLI) to enable verbose SSH output. The raw ssh -v output is shown in the detail pane after connecting, which exposes handshake details, key negotiation, and authentication steps.

docs.title: Persistent State (~/.susshi_state.json)
docs.text:
susshi writes state to ~/.susshi_state.json after each session. The file contains:

Key Description favorites Set of server names marked as favorites expanded_items Set of group/environment names that are expanded in the tree sort_mode Current sort (alphabetical or recent-first) last_seen Map of server_name → ISO timestamp of last connection command_history Last 100 ad-hoc commands (deduplicated) tunnel_overrides User-created or user-edited tunnels per server

To reset all state: rm ~/.susshi_state.json

To reset only tunnel overrides without losing favorites, edit the file and clear the tunnel_overrides key.

docs.title: Connection fails immediately
docs.text:
1. Enable verbose mode (v) and retry — the SSH handshake error appears in the detail pane.
  2. Check that ssh_key exists and is readable (ls -la ~/.ssh/id_ed25519).
  3. If using jump mode, verify the jump host is reachable independently: ssh jump-user@jump.example.com.
  4. If use_system_ssh_config: true is set, check ~/.ssh/config for conflicting Host blocks.

docs.title: Config file not loading
docs.text: Run susshi --validate to check all config files for syntax errors, unknown fields, and unresolved includes. Errors and warnings are printed with file names and line numbers.

docs.title: Wallix connection hangs or shows the raw menu
docs.text: Declare the server authorization in wallix.authorizations so susshi connects directly without the menu. See docs/wallix.md for the full troubleshooting guide (Cible invalide, signature algorithm not supported, tunnels).

docs.title: SCP fails or a tunnel stops
docs.text: The SCP result popup and the tunnel status show the message returned by ssh/scp (OpenSSH warnings removed). In Wallix mode the SCP error also shows the exact target used, to compare with a manual scp.

docs.title: Clipboard copy (y) shows a fallback overlay
docs.text:
The clipboard backend is unavailable. Install the required tool for your environment:

  • X11: xclip or xsel
  • Wayland: wl-clipboard (provides wl-copy)
  • macOS: built-in (should work out of the box)

The fallback overlay displays the full SSH command — select and copy it manually.

docs.title: TUI looks garbled or colors are wrong
docs.text:
susshi requires a truecolor terminal (24-bit color). Verify with:

echo $COLORTERM   # should output "truecolor" or "24bit"

Common terminals with truecolor: Alacritty, kitty, WezTerm, iTerm2, modern GNOME Terminal.

docs.title: Mouse click does not work
docs.text: Press M to toggle mouse capture. When mouse capture is disabled, terminal text selection works normally but TUI click events are not processed.

docs.title: TUI Guide
docs.text: susshi provides an interactive terminal UI for browsing and connecting to servers.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
Key Action j / ↓ Move down k / ↑ Move up Space Expand/collapse group Enter Connect / toggle group q Quit

Mouse:

  • Click: select item.
  • Double-click: connect.

docs.title: Search and Filters
docs.text:
Key Action / Enter search mode Ctrl+U Clear search query Esc Cancel search

Search behavior:

  • Matches server name and hostname.
  • Supports tag filters with #tag tokens.
  • Multiple tags are AND-combined.
  • Mixed queries are allowed (api #prod).
  • defaults.default_filter pre-applies a startup filter.

docs.title: Connection Controls
docs.text:
Key Action Tab Cycle mode (Direct/Jump/Wallix) 1 Select Direct 2 Select Jump 3 Select Wallix v Toggle verbose SSH mode y Copy generated SSH command

If the clipboard is unavailable (headless session, missing wl-clipboard, etc.), an overlay displays the command for manual copy. Dismiss with Enter or Esc.

docs.title: Mode-dependent details
docs.text:
The detail panel only shows the connection settings of the selected mode:

Mode Extra lines Direct none Jump Jump: — the jump host (jump) Wallix Wallix: — bastion_user@bastion, and Authorization: (see below)

The Wallix Authorization: line follows the same resolution as SCP, tunnels, ad-hoc commands and diagnostics:

  • declared authorizations (wallix.authorization, then wallix.authorizations), in the order they are tried;
  • otherwise the name derived from the YAML structure, marked (derived);
  • otherwise Wallix menu: the selection is made in the bastion menu when connecting.

Nothing is shown when the selected mode is Jump or Wallix but the server has no jump host or bastion configured.

docs.title: Productivity Features
docs.text:
Key Action r Hot-reload all config files f Toggle favorite F Favorites-only view C Collapse all groups/environments/namespaces E Expand all groups/environments/namespaces Ctrl+Y Cycle Catppuccin theme variant (Latte → Frappe → Macchiato → Mocha → …) H Toggle recent-sort view h Toggle keyboard help overlay o Open group overview dashboard \| Pin/unpin server in split pane

State is persisted in ~/.susshi_state.json (favorites, expanded nodes, sort mode, last seen connection timestamps, tunnel overrides).

docs.title: Server Notes
docs.text:
Add a free-form notes field to any server in the YAML config:

servers:
  - name: web-01
    host: 192.168.1.10
    notes: "staging — reboot window Thursday nights"

The note is displayed in the detail panel below the last-seen timestamp.

docs.title: Diagnostics and Commands
docs.text:
Key Action d Run quick diagnostics on the selected server x Run ad-hoc SSH command on the selected server p Prompt for SSH credential (passphrase if a key is configured, password otherwise) M Toggle mouse capture (disable to allow terminal text selection)

Diagnostics include:

  • Kernel, OS info, CPU model/core count, load average.
  • RAM and disk usage bars.
  • Extra filesystem checks from probe_filesystems.

Ad-hoc command output is displayed in the detail pane (up to 20 lines) with colored exit status.

Both x and d use the current connection mode (Direct, Jump or Wallix), with the server's ssh_options. They run non-interactively (BatchMode=yes): authentication must not require a prompt.

docs.title: Command history
docs.text: When the ad-hoc command prompt (x) is open, use ↑ and ↓ to navigate previously run commands. The history is deduplicated (identical consecutive commands are not duplicated) and persists across sessions (saved in ~/.susshi_state.json, capped at 100 entries).

docs.title: Group Overview Dashboard
docs.text:
Press o when a group or environment header is selected to open the overview dashboard.

susshi launches a parallel SSH probe on every server in the group and displays results in a live-updating overlay:

Column Description ✓ / ✗ Connection success or failure Name Server name Host SSH hostname Status Load average, RAM %, disk % on success; first line of error message on failure
  • Results arrive as threads complete; pending servers show ….
  • Use j/↓ and k/↑ to scroll the list.
  • Press o again or Esc to close.

The probe uses the current connection mode (Direct/Jump) selected in the tab bar.

docs.title: Split Pane
docs.text:
Press | on any server to pin it to a dedicated right panel.

The layout switches from a 2-column view (tree + details) to a 3-column view (tree + current details + pinned server). The pinned server panel shows name, host, user, port, group/environment, and connection mode.

Press | again on the same server (or on any non-server item) to unpin and return to the standard layout.

docs.title: Tunnels and SCP
docs.text:
Key Action T Open SSH tunnel manager s Open SCP transfer form

See tunnels.md and scp.md for full details.

docs.title: Keyboard Help Overlay
docs.text: Press h at any time to open an in-TUI reference of all keybindings. Press h again or Esc to close it.

docs.title: Error Overlay
docs.text:
Connection errors are shown as an in-TUI overlay.

Dismiss with Enter, Esc, or q.

docs.title: SSH Tunnels
docs.text: susshi supports SSH local-port-forwarding tunnels, configured per-server and managed interactively from the TUI.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Define tunnels in the YAML config at any level (defaults, group, environment, server). A tunnels list at a lower level replaces the one inherited from above.

servers:
  - name: db-01
    host: 198.51.100.11
    tunnels:
      - local_port: 5432
        remote_host: 127.0.0.1
        remote_port: 5432
        label: "PostgreSQL"
      - local_port: 6379
        remote_host: 127.0.0.1
        remote_port: 6379
        label: "Redis"

Each entry produces: ssh -L <local_port>:<remote_host>:<remote_port> -N …

Fields:

Field Required Description local_port Yes Port bound on localhost remote_host Yes Host as seen from the remote server (usually 127.0.0.1) remote_port Yes Port on the remote side label No Display name shown in the TUI tunnel list

Wallix mode: tunnels require the server's Wallix authorization to be known from the configuration (wallix.authorization, or a single entry in wallix.authorizations, see Wallix Guide); without it, Wallix shows its selection menu, which a background tunnel cannot answer. susshi runs ssh -A -T -L <local_port>:<server FQDN>:<remote_port> -l user@target+SSH+AUTHORIZATION+bastion_user bastion and keeps the remote shell session open in the background: Wallix closes the connection when port forwarding is requested outside an open session on the target, so -N cannot be used. A local remote_host (127.0.0.1, localhost, ::1) is replaced by the server FQDN, as documented by the bastion. If the bastion refuses the tunnel, its message is shown in the tunnel status. Port forwarding through the bastion is not necessarily enabled by default on every environment: ask the bastion administrator to enable it if needed (the TUI tunnel list shows this reminder in Wallix mode).

docs.title: keep_open
docs.text:
Set keep_open: true at any config level to automatically reopen the TUI after a connection closes. Useful when you want to run a tunnel, disconnect, and immediately pick another server.

defaults:
  keep_open: false  # default

docs.title: TUI Tunnel Manager
docs.text:
Press T in the TUI to open the tunnel manager overlay.

Actions:

Key Action Enter Start or stop the selected tunnel a Add a new tunnel (user override) e Edit the selected tunnel D Delete the selected tunnel Esc Close the tunnel manager

Active tunnels show a live status badge next to the server name in the tree.

docs.title: User Overrides
docs.text: Tunnels added or edited through the TUI are stored as user overrides in ~/.susshi_state.json. Overrides persist across restarts and are merged with config-defined tunnels at runtime. Deleting an override reverts the server to its config-defined tunnels.

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text: Concrete susshi configurations for common infrastructure setups.

docs.title: Team managing a large server fleet
docs.text:
When your ~/.ssh/config grows beyond a few dozen hosts, susshi's hierarchical inventory keeps things navigable.

defaults:
  user: "ops"
  ssh_key: "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"

groups:
  - name: "Production"
    tags: ["prod"]
    servers:
      - name: "api-01"
        host: "10.0.1.10"
        tags: ["api", "critical"]
      - name: "api-02"
        host: "10.0.1.11"
        tags: ["api", "critical"]
      - name: "db-primary"
        host: "10.0.2.10"
        tags: ["db", "critical"]

  - name: "Staging"
    tags: ["staging"]
    servers:
      - name: "api-staging"
        host: "10.1.1.10"
        tags: ["api"]

Use #prod or #api #critical in the / search bar to filter instantly. Star frequently-used servers with f and toggle the favorites-only view with F.

docs.title: Multi-hop jump hosts
docs.text:
Connect through one or more bastion hosts without writing manual ProxyJump chains.

defaults:
  user: "ops"
  ssh_key: "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"

groups:
  - name: "Internal (via bastion)"
    jump:
      - host: "bastion.example.com"
        user: "jump-user"
        ssh_key: "~/.ssh/jump_key"
    servers:
      - name: "internal-db"
        host: "172.16.0.10"
        mode: "jump"
      - name: "internal-api"
        host: "172.16.0.20"
        mode: "jump"

susshi builds the full ProxyJump chain automatically. Override mode on any individual server to bypass the jump for that host.

docs.title: Three-hop chain
docs.text:
jump:
  - host: "public-bastion.example.com"
    user: "jump1"
  - host: "internal-bastion.corp"
    user: "jump2"

docs.title: Wallix bastion
docs.text:
For teams using a Wallix bastion, declare the authorizations per environment: susshi then connects directly to the target, and SCP and tunnels go through the bastion too.

defaults:
  user: "ops"
  ssh_key: "~/.ssh/wallix_key"
  mode: "wallix"
  wallix:
    host: "wallix.corp.internal"
    user: "ops"
    group: "ops-admins"                 # shared authorization suffix

groups:
  - name: "SHOP"
    environments:
      - name: "PR"
        wallix:
          authorizations: ["PR-SHOP_{group}"]   # → PR-SHOP_ops-admins
        servers:
          - name: "web-01"
            host: "pr-web-01.shop.corp.internal"
          - name: "db-01"
            host: "pr-db-01.shop.corp.internal"

Without a declared authorization, susshi falls back to the Wallix menu and selects the matching entry. See Wallix bastion for the resolution order, the menu flow and troubleshooting.

docs.title: Multi-environment with variable inheritance
docs.text:
Avoid duplicating connection settings across staging, pre-prod, and production.

defaults:
  user: "deploy"
  ssh_key: "~/.ssh/deploy_key"

groups:
  - name: "App Cluster"
    environments:
      - name: "staging"
        ssh_key: "~/.ssh/staging_key"
        servers:
          - name: "app-staging-01"
            host: "staging-01.internal"
      - name: "production"
        servers:
          - name: "app-prod-01"
            host: "prod-01.internal"
          - name: "app-prod-02"
            host: "prod-02.internal"

The staging environment overrides only ssh_key; all other settings inherit from defaults. Switch modes with Tab if a server supports both direct and jump access.

docs.title: SSH tunnels for development
docs.text:
Forward a remote service port to localhost without keeping a terminal open.

defaults:
  user: "dev"

groups:
  - name: "Dev tunnels"
    servers:
      - name: "remote-postgres"
        host: "dev-db.example.com"
        mode: "direct"
        tunnels:
          - local_port: 5433
            remote_host: "localhost"
            remote_port: 5432

Open the tunnel manager with T, start/stop tunnels without disconnecting. Tunnel state persists between susshi sessions.

docs.title: SCP file transfers
docs.text:
Transfer files to/from any server in your inventory with s (SCP mode).

Useful for:

  • Uploading config files to multiple servers
  • Retrieving logs without rsync setup
  • Copying build artifacts to a staging server

See SCP Transfers for full usage.

docs.title: Ansible export
docs.text:
Once your inventory is in susshi, export it to Ansible format:

susshi --export ansible > inventory.yml

Other export formats: --export terraform, --export nmap, --export csv, --export openssh.

See Import & Export for details.

docs.title: Import from ~/.ssh/config
docs.text:
Migrate your existing SSH config into susshi in one step:

susshi --import-ssh-config

susshi reads ~/.ssh/config, groups hosts by their Match / Host blocks, and writes a ~/.susshi.yml skeleton that you can refine.

docs.title: Wallix Guide
docs.text: This page describes how susshi behaves in wallix mode.

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
defaults:
  wallix:
    host: "bastion.example.com"
    user: "bastion-user"
    group: "devops-admins"
    account: "default"
    protocol: "SSH"
    auto_select: true
    fail_if_menu_match_error: true
    selection_timeout_secs: 8

Enable Wallix on a server:

- name: "internal-nas"
  host: "198.51.100.200"
  mode: "wallix"

docs.title: Declaring Authorizations (recommended)
docs.text:
Declare the Wallix authorizations in the configuration so susshi never has to guess. wallix.authorizations is a list inherited like any other Wallix field (defaults → group → environment → server, the most specific level wins). {group} is replaced by the resolved wallix.group suffix:

defaults:
  wallix:
    host: "ssh.bastion.example"
    user: "jdoe"
    group: "ces3s-admins"            # suffix shared by every authorization

groups:
  - name: "COLIBRIS"
    environments:
      - name: "PR"
        wallix:
          authorizations:
            - "PR-COLIBRIS_{group}"  # → PR-COLIBRIS_ces3s-admins
      - name: "PP - BaS"
        wallix:
          authorizations:            # several candidates, in order of preference
            - "PP-COLIBRIS_{group}"
            - "PP-BAS_{group}"

Resolution order (interactive SSH, SCP, tunnels, ad-hoc commands and diagnostics):

  1. wallix.authorization — exact name, always first ({group} is not replaced there).
  2. wallix.authorizations — declared candidates, in order.
  3. Last resort: detection — the name derived from the YAML structure (<ENV>-<GROUP>_<group>), then the Wallix menu.

An entry containing {group} is ignored when no wallix.group is resolved.

Tip: the authorization names are listed in the Wallix menu (Autorisation column) when you connect to the bastion without a target.

In Wallix mode, the TUI detail panel shows the resolved authorization (Authorization: line): the declared names, the derived name marked (derived), or Wallix menu when nothing is known. See tui.md.

docs.title: Direct login (authorization known)
docs.text:
When exactly one authorization is known from the configuration, susshi connects directly:

ssh -A -l "user@target+SSH+AUTHORIZATION+bastion_user" bastion

There is no menu probe and no PTY relay: ssh drives the terminal itself. Agent forwarding (-A) lets the bastion authenticate on the target with your SSH agent, so your key must be loaded in the agent (ssh-add -l).

docs.title: Menu flow (last resort)
docs.text:
Without a single known authorization (none, or several candidates), susshi goes through the Wallix menu: it opens the bastion session in a PTY, parses the menu, selects the matching entry, then relays the session to your terminal. Declared candidates are tried first when matching the menu, then the detected names.

The relay puts your terminal in raw mode and forwards window resizes, so Tab completion, arrow keys, Ctrl+R/Ctrl+C and full-screen tools (vim, less, top) behave as in a plain ssh session.

docs.title: Group Inheritance and Override
docs.text:
wallix.group follows the same inheritance model as other susshi settings.

  • If server.wallix.group is set, it has priority.
  • Otherwise susshi uses the inherited group from environment/group/defaults.
  • If no group can be resolved, susshi switches to targeted fallback selection.

Example:

defaults:
  wallix:
    host: "bastion.example.com"
    user: "wallix-user"
    group: "devops-admins"

groups:
  - name: "Databases"
    servers:
      - name: "db-ops-01"
        host: "db-ops-01.internal.example"
        mode: "wallix"
        wallix:
          group: "qa-admins"

docs.title: SSH user identity
docs.text:
In the menu flow, susshi builds the SSH User field as:

<wallix_user>@<target_fqdn>:SSH[:<ENV_GROUP>]:<wallix_user>

Where:

  • <target_fqdn> comes from the selected server host.
  • <ENV_GROUP> is included only when a deterministic authorization group is resolved.
  • If resolution is ambiguous, susshi avoids generating a potentially wrong authorization silently.

docs.title: Selection strategy
docs.text:
susshi computes candidates before selecting an ID in the Wallix menu:

  • Target candidates: FQDN, short host, and structure-derived aliases.
  • Authorization candidates: declared authorization / authorizations first, then wallix.group and structure-derived variants.
  • Prefixed authorizations are supported (for example, ST-ANSIBLE_devops-admins matches devops-admins).

docs.title: Targeted fallback popup
docs.text:
When automatic resolution fails (no match or ambiguity), susshi opens a focused popup instead of exposing the full global menu flow.

  • Candidate entries are pre-filtered against the current target server.
  • Search starts from the target hostname to reduce noise.
  • The selected Wallix entry ID is cached for the current session.
  • During nominal flow, the global pseudo-TTY menu output stays hidden.

docs.title: Pagination and fallback
docs.text:
• Paginated menus are scanned automatically (page X/Y, then n).
  • If Wallix asks for a secondary prompt like Adresse cible, susshi auto-fills the configured server host.
  • If no reliable match is found, susshi falls back to manual in-session selection.

docs.title: Direct connection mode (direct)
docs.text:
wallix.direct: true skips the menu probe in the menu flow, for targets that Wallix always connects directly without presenting a selection menu. It has no effect when an authorization is known from the configuration — the direct login is used anyway.

defaults:
  wallix:
    host: "bastion.example.com"
    user: "bastion-user"
    direct: true          # skip menu probe — Wallix connects directly

docs.title: Forcing a Specific Authorization
docs.text:
When a server needs an authorization that does not follow the shared {group} suffix (for example a …_crtech-admins authorization on a single server), set wallix.authorization to the exact name shown in the Wallix menu:

groups:
  - name: "Secured Perimeter"
    servers:
      - name: "anscore02"
        host: "anscore02.internal.example"
        mode: "wallix"
        wallix:
          authorization: "STI-ANSCORE_crtech-admins"  # exact name from the Wallix menu

authorization takes priority over authorizations and group. It is passed verbatim in the direct login string, so the connection opens immediately without going through the menu. When the name follows the shared suffix, prefer authorizations: ["STI-ANSCORE_{group}"].

docs.title: SCP and Tunnels
docs.text:
• SCP (scp.md) goes through the system scp binary with the direct login: scp -A … user@target+SSH+AUTHORIZATION+bastion_user@bastion:path. Declared authorizations are tried in order, moving to the next one while Wallix answers Cible invalide; the derived name is the last resort.
  • Tunnels (tunnels.md) require a known authorization (a background tunnel cannot answer the menu). susshi runs ssh -A -T -L … and keeps a shell session open on the target, because Wallix closes the connection when port forwarding is requested outside an open session. Port forwarding is not necessarily enabled on every environment: ask the bastion administrator if needed.

docs.title: Commands and Diagnostics
docs.text:
The ad-hoc command (x) and the diagnostic probe (d) use the same direct login as SCP, trying the authorization candidates in order while Wallix answers Cible invalide.

The command is not sent as an SSH exec request (the remote command subprotocol is often not granted by the authorization): susshi opens a shell session without PTY (ssh -A -T) and writes the command on its standard input, followed by an end marker carrying the exit code and exit. The bastion does not always close the session when the remote shell ends, so susshi stops the session as soon as the marker is received. The output is that of your login shell on the target; the probe ignores anything printed before its own output (banner, shell startup files).

Timeouts: 120 s for an ad-hoc command, 30 s for a diagnostic. Past that, ssh is killed and the partial output is shown in the error.

docs.title: Behavior Controls
docs.text:
• authorizations: candidate authorization names, in order; {group} is replaced by group.
  • authorization: exact Wallix authorization name — highest priority, pins the entry.
  • auto_select: enable automatic selection attempts (menu flow).
  • fail_if_menu_match_error: keep trying (including pagination) before falling back (menu flow).
  • selection_timeout_secs: menu parsing timeout budget (menu flow).
  • direct: skip the menu probe (menu flow only).
  • header_columns: list of tokens used to detect and skip the menu header line. Default: ["ID", "Cible", "Autorisation"]. Override if your bastion shows column headers in a different language:
defaults:
  wallix:
    header_columns: ["Num", "Target", "Authorization"]

docs.title: Cible invalide
docs.text:
Wallix rejects the target/authorization pair in the login string.

  • Check the authorization name against the Autorisation column of the Wallix menu.
  • Check that host is the name Wallix knows for the target (usually the FQDN).
  • For SCP, ad-hoc commands and diagnostics, the error lists every target that was tried.

docs.title: signature algorithm not supported
docs.text:
The bastion signs with ssh-rsa (SHA-1), refused by default by recent OpenSSH. Allow it for susshi connections:

defaults:
  ssh_options:
    - "PubkeyAcceptedKeyTypes=+ssh-rsa"

docs.title: Tunnel stops right after starting
docs.text:
• The authorization may not allow port forwarding: ask the bastion administrator.
  • The tunnel status shows the message returned by ssh / the bastion.

docs.title: No matching authorization (menu flow)
docs.text:
• Declare the authorization in wallix.authorizations (see above).
  • Otherwise verify wallix.group at defaults/group/environment/server level and ensure the target host in config matches the Wallix entry target naming.
  • If still unresolved, use the popup and keep the selected entry for the current session.

docs.title: Ambiguous authorization (menu flow)
docs.text:
• Multiple authorizations can match the same server target.
  • susshi will not guess silently and opens the targeted popup.
  • Declare the right one in wallix.authorizations, or set wallix.authorization on the server.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Wallix mode can be inherited from defaults/group/environment.
  • ControlMaster multiplexing is silently disabled in Wallix mode.
  • Wallix mode is Unix-only.
